key_insight: At affordable mesh resolution, brittle-fracture models for cooled dark chocolate cannot practically match elastic slope, peak force and crack path with a single parameter set, so calibration must prioritize a stated objective.
engineering_relevance: Objective-specific fracture calibration can support simulations of food breakage during production, transport, cutting and mastication.
method: Compare sharp-interface and diffuse phase-field frameworks for Griffith-type brittle fracture.
Identify elastic parameters from pre-crack tension and compression, then critical energy release rate from three-point-bending peak force.
Calibrate phase-field width last and report the calibration objective, numerical parameters and boundary value problem.
evidence_signal: The assessment uses cooled dark chocolate as a reproducible model material and evaluates elastic response, bending peak force and crack behavior at affordable spatial discretization.
watch_item: Mesh resolution constrains the minimum phase-field width, which can alter structural response, crack curvature and stress fields.
paper_title: Finite Element Modeling of Fracture in Brittle Foods with Physically Consistent Parameter Calibration: A Practical Case Study on Cooled Dark Chocolate
